scenario.draft: Test a member's ability to perform advanced filtering on their notifications: filter by type (e.g., mention, reply, system), delivery status, or unread status. Generate multiple notifications with different types/statuses, then use PATCH to retrieve filtered lists and validate correct pagination and filtering.

dependencies.purpose: Register a member to generate and search notifications for.
Admin creates notifications of various types for the member; these will be used as filter targets.

scenario.draft: Test that a moderator can retrieve a paginated list of all system notices, regardless of active/inactive/scheduled status. First, ensure that there are system notices with different statuses: active, inactive, scheduled for the future, and expired. The test should check that all such notices (including future and expired) are visible to a moderator, verify correct pagination, and confirm that each returned notice contains all required metadata fields (category linkage, title, body, status, activation window, timestamps).

dependencies.purpose: Create system notices in various states: active, inactive, expired, and scheduled future, to ensure all status types are covered for the moderator's view.

scenario.draft: Test that category-based filtering and pagination work for the moderator system notices listing. First, create a system notice associated with a specific category and others that are global. The test should call the GET endpoint with filtering (if query parameters supported), and verify category-specific and global notices are correctly returned and paginated, including scenarios where there are enough notices to trigger multiple pages.

dependencies.purpose: Create at least one notice linked to a specific category and several global notices to verify category-filtering and pagination behaviors.
Create a category in the board to use as the parent for category-limited notices.

scenario.draft: Test that, as a guest (non-authenticated user), only public, currently active, scheduled system notices are returned, and sensitive or inactive notices are not. Create a mix of active, inactive, scheduled, and expired notices. Access the GET endpoint as a guest and verify only public, currently active/scheduled notices are returned and others are filtered out.

dependencies.purpose: Create system notices in all relevant statuses for validation against expected guest visibility.

scenario.draft: Verify that an admin can search system notices using advanced filters such as status (active/inactive), scheduled windows (start_at/end_at), and text matching on title or body. Set up a variety of notices with different activation windows and statuses. Perform PATCH search queries that target each filter condition. Confirm that the returned paginated list matches criteria accurately, and out-of-range or no-match queries return empty results.

dependencies.purpose: Create system notices in various statuses and scheduled intervals to match multiple filter criteria.

scenario.draft: Ensure that moderators can use text search and category-based filters when searching system notices. Create several system notices, some global and some tied to categories, with diverse titles and body content. Issue a PATCH search filtering by keywords and category_id, and validate results include only matching notices. Test negative scenarios where search criteria return no results.

dependencies.purpose: Create a diverse set of system notices for search and filtering tests.
Create categories to use as parents for category-specific notices.

scenario.draft: Test that an admin can retrieve details for any system notice, regardless of whether it is active, inactive, expired, or scheduled for the future. Create notices with each of these statuses, then invoke the GET endpoint for each notice's ID. Verify that all fields (including category linkage, scheduling, status, and all timestamps) are present and correctly represent the stored values. Check handling of valid and non-existent IDs (404 error expected).

dependencies.purpose: Create one active, one inactive, one scheduled, and one expired system notice to be used for detail retrieval.

scenario.draft: Verify a moderator can fetch full details for system notices that are inactive or scheduled (not public), as well as active ones. Create a system notice in each state (active, inactive, scheduled, expired), then fetch each individually using the moderator GET endpoint and confirm all attributes are shown. Also check that requesting a non-existent notice ID returns a not-found error.

dependencies.purpose: Create system notices across all relevant statuses to test visibility for a moderator.

scenario.draft: Verify that an admin can retrieve all attachments for an existing comment created by a member. First, create a member and have them create a comment on an existing post. Add one or more attachments to the comment. Then, as an admin, fetch the attachments for the comment and ensure all added files are present with correct metadata (file name, MIME type, uploader, timestamp).

dependencies.purpose: Create a member user who will author the comment.
Create a new comment on an existing post as the member. Requires valid post and member IDs.
Attach one or more files to the comment to ensure there are records to retrieve.

scenario.draft: Verify that fetching attachments for a non-existent (invalid UUID) comment as an admin returns a not found error. This ensures proper error handling and prevents data leaks.
Validate that an unauthorized user (non-admin) cannot access the list of attachments for a comment that belongs to another user, ensuring access control policies are enforced.

dependencies.purpose: Create two member accounts to simulate unrelated user access.
One user creates a comment, and another tries to access its attachments via the admin endpoint, which should raise permission errors for non-admins.

scenario.draft: Test that a member can filter their comment's attachments using filters such as file name, uploader, and MIME type. Add several attachments with varying properties and then perform filtered searches. Verify correct pagination and filtering is applied as per input.

dependencies.purpose: Create a comment as a member.
Upload several attachments for complex filtering and paging tests.

scenario.draft: Ensure the search API for comment attachments supports correct pagination and sorting. Add more files than the default page size, use pagination parameters, and confirm the results respect both limits and sorting orders.

dependencies.purpose: Create a comment as a member.
Upload more attachments than the typical page size to test pagination and sorting.

scenario.draft: Validate that a member who is not the comment's author cannot search attachments for a comment they do not own. As one member, attempt to run the search API for another member's comment; the API should deny access.

dependencies.purpose: Create two distinct member users.
First member creates a comment. Second member attempts to search its attachments.

scenario.draft: Confirm that a moderator can search and filter attachments for any comment, regardless of ownership. Moderators should be able to use all filtering options (uploader, MIME type, file name, date) to audit and review attachments across the board.

dependencies.purpose: Create a member and moderator user.
Member creates a comment with attachments.
Upload attachments to the member comment.

scenario.draft: Verify that an admin can perform filtered, paginated searches on attachments for any comment, validating both correct filter application and that no attachments are visible from restricted, non-existent, or unauthorized comments. Ensure security and privacy policies are correctly implemented.

dependencies.purpose: Create a member and an admin account.
The member creates comments with varying numbers of attachments.
Upload attachments with differing MIME types, names, and uploaders.

scenario.draft: Ensure that a comment owner can retrieve full metadata details for a specific attachment on their comment. The metadata must include the file URI, file name, MIME type, uploader ID, and timestamps, confirming all information was stored correctly upon upload.

dependencies.purpose: Create a new comment as a member.
Upload an attachment to the comment to acquire a valid attachment ID.

scenario.draft: Confirm that a member who is not the comment's owner cannot access details of attachments belonging to another user's comment. The system should deny access and return the correct error code to prevent unauthorized data exposure.

dependencies.purpose: Create two member users.
First member creates a comment with attachments.

scenario.draft: Attempt to fetch details for an attachment using an invalid or non-related attachmentId. The API should return an error specifying that the attachment does not exist or does not belong to the given comment, verifying referential integrity enforcement.

dependencies.purpose: Create a comment as a member for which attachments are referenced.

scenario.draft: Test fetching notification details for a notificationId when the requesting user is the recipient. First, create a member and trigger a notification (e.g., via post reply or by direct notification using the admin/notification creation endpoint). Attempt to fetch the notification using the recipient's session and confirm that all detailed fields are returned, including message, type, status, delivery/read timestamps, and context as per the schema. The business rule ensuring recipient-only access must be validated.

dependencies.purpose: Create a notification event for a specific member to ensure there is a notificationId to retrieve. This sets up the context for access control and data presence.

scenario.draft: Test that a notification cannot be retrieved by a user who is not the recipient. First, create two distinct member accounts and generate a notification for only one of them. Attempt to access the notification's details as a different member and verify that access is denied with the proper error response (e.g., 403/404), ensuring strict privacy and business rule enforcement.

dependencies.purpose: Create the notification for the first member to be used in the access control test.

scenario.draft: Test successful creation of a new notification event for a member by an admin. The admin provides all required fields: recipient member ID, content message, type (reply, mention, etc.), delivery status, and optional context. Verify that the notification is correctly saved, associated with the correct recipient, and that audit logs would be updated. Validate that only allowed roles (admin) can create notifications via this endpoint.

Test creation of a notification using an invalid or non-existent member ID. Verify that the creation fails with a proper error message, and that no notification is generated in the database. Check for system audit of failed attempts and that there are no side effects.

Verify that a moderator can successfully create a notification for a member. Supply valid member ID, content, type, and delivery parameters. Check that the notification is persisted, assigned to the correct recipient, and that the moderator's identity is appropriately recorded in audit trails. Access must only be granted for authorized roles.

Attempt to create a notification using this endpoint with a role that is neither moderator nor admin. Ensure that access is denied, and an appropriate authorization error is returned, confirming that business logic restricts creation accordingly.

Test that a member can mark their own notification as read using this endpoint. After creating a notification (using admin or moderator creation endpoint), call this update as the recipient. Confirm that the notification's read_at timestamp updates, status reflects the change, and audit log (if visible) records the update.

dependencies.purpose: Create the notification for the recipient member to enable the update scenario.

scenario.draft: Test that a member cannot update a notification that does not belong to them. Create a notification for one member, then attempt to perform the update as a different member. Expect an error response (403/404), verifying strict recipient-only update rights for notifications.

dependencies.purpose: Generate a notification assigned to another member for update access test.

scenario.draft: Test that an admin can update notification properties for any recipient. This may include marking as read, updating the message content, changing delivery status, or addressing delivery failure. Create a notification, then as admin, perform various allowed updates and verify the persisted changes. Audit logging should reflect the admin action, and system integrity must be maintained.

dependencies.purpose: Create a notification as the basis for admin update actions.

scenario.draft: Attempt to perform an update as admin on a non-existent notificationId. Ensure the operation fails with a not-found error and check that no accidental record or system side effect is introduced by the invalid update attempt.

Verify that a moderator can view the detailed metadata of a specific attachment linked to a comment. Scenario: Create a member, create a comment under a post, upload an attachment as the member, then use moderator privileges to retrieve this attachment's metadata using its attachmentId and associated commentId. Confirm all metadata (file name, URI, uploader, mime type, timestamps) matches expected input. This checks correct role-based read access and the referential integrity of attachment metadata for moderation.

dependencies.purpose: Create/register a new board member (the original uploader/author of the attachment).
Create a new comment as the registered member so that an attachment can be linked to it.
Upload a new file attachment to the comment created above; returns attachmentId and associates metadata.

scenario.draft: Test the case where a moderator attempts to retrieve details for a non-existent attachmentId under a valid commentId. After creating a comment as a member, attempt to fetch with a random (non-existent) attachmentId and expect a 404 not found error. This ensures proper error handling and no information leakage about deleted or unknown files.

dependencies.purpose: Create/register a new member (comment/post owner).
Create a test comment to produce a valid commentId for testing.

scenario.draft: Verify that unauthorized users (such as non-owners, non-moderators, or guests) cannot view the detailed metadata of an attachment on a comment that is not theirs. This checks role-based access control enforcement for sensitive or private attachments.

dependencies.purpose: Register a legitimate board member (as the attachment owner).
Let the owner create a comment for attachment upload.
Owner uploads attachment to the comment.

scenario.draft: Verify that an admin user can retrieve detailed information about a comment attachment, regardless of who uploaded the file. Scenario: Register a new member, create a comment as that member, have them upload an attachment, then access the attachment detail as admin. Checks for correct access and metadata integrity.

dependencies.purpose: Create a test member who will upload the attachment.
Member creates a comment for attachment.
Upload the attachment (to be accessed as admin).

scenario.draft: Test the case where an admin requests an attachmentId that does not exist under a comment. After registering a member and creating their comment, try a random UUID as attachmentId and assert that a 404 or not found error is returned. Verifies proper not-found error handling and no leakage of metadata.

dependencies.purpose: Add a test board member.
Create a comment to act as a valid context.

scenario.draft: Ensure that if a regular member attempts to retrieve an attachment not owned by them (without admin privileges), the request is denied. This tests enforcement of strict access control for viewing attachment metadata at the admin path.

dependencies.purpose: Register both an uploader (owner) and a second, non-owner member.
Owner creates comment for attachment.
Owner uploads an attachment linked to their comment.

scenario.draft: A registered member adds a valid file attachment to their own comment. Scenario: Register a member, create a comment, upload an allowed file type via this endpoint, and verify the returned metadata matches input (file name, MIME type, uploader ID, URI). Confirms attachment is linked to the comment and retrievable by the member.

dependencies.purpose: Register new member for attachment upload.
Create a comment using the registered member.

scenario.draft: Try to upload a file attachment as a member to a non-existent commentId. Expects a 404 or error response, verifying the system does not allow orphaned attachments and checks for valid foreign key constraints.

dependencies.purpose: Prepare an authenticated member for request.

scenario.draft: Verify that a member cannot add attachments to another member's comment. Register two members; one creates a comment, and the second attempts to add an attachment to it. Request should be denied (forbidden) and logged as an unauthorized action.

dependencies.purpose: Register both owner and secondary member users.
Let owner create the target comment.

scenario.draft: Test business rules on allowed file types: attempt to add a file with a disallowed MIME type or extension, and verify that the operation fails with a clear error. Confirms that server-side content-type validation prevents unsupported formats (e.g., blocked executables or scripts).

dependencies.purpose: Prepare a member for attachment upload testing.
Create a member's comment to hold attachments.

scenario.draft: Verify the moderator can add an attachment to any comment (including comments not owned by them): register a member, create a comment as a member, then add an attachment as moderator. Checks cross-role assignment and audit capturing. Response should confirm correct association of metadata and permissions.

dependencies.purpose: Register a member user to act as comment author.
Create a comment with the member's credentials.

scenario.draft: Attempt to add an attachment to a non-existent commentId as a moderator. Should receive an error (not found), verifying the system enforces valid parent comment existence for all uploads regardless of role.

Try to upload a file with a blocked/unsupported MIME type as a moderator. Validates moderation interface is subject to the same file validation logic as member uploader, denying non-compliant file formats.

dependencies.purpose: Ensure a target comment exists by registering a member author.
Member creates a comment to serve as upload parent.

scenario.draft: Test that an admin can upload and associate an attachment with any comment—even if not the original author—bypassing member-level restrictions. Register a member, have the member create a comment, then perform the upload as admin. Validate that response metadata is correct and that audit information records the admin as uploader.

dependencies.purpose: Register a member (acts as comment author).
Comment created by member for admin to upload against.

scenario.draft: Admin attempts to upload an attachment to a non-existent commentId. Expect a not found or error response. Verifies admin interface applies required referential checks, no matter the user role.

Admin attempts to upload a restricted file type; ensure upload is rejected and error message is returned. Confirms that even admin uploads are restricted by security/content validation logic for attachment file types.

dependencies.purpose: Register a member to ensure a valid target comment exists.
Valid comment is created by member, with admin acting as uploader.

scenario.draft: Test successful update of a board member's audit or registration data by an admin. First, ensure a valid member exists by creating a member record. As an admin, perform a PUT request with updated suspension status (e.g., setting the suspended_at field), join time correction, or user_identifier change. Confirm that the response reflects the updated fields and includes proper audit logging. Validate that only allowed fields are updated and that the member's record is otherwise unchanged.

dependencies.purpose: Create a test member record to be used as the target for the update scenario, ensuring there is a valid memberId.

scenario.draft: Test update failure when an admin tries to update a member using an invalid or non-existent memberId. Attempt a PUT with a random or malformed UUID as the memberId path parameter. Expect the system to return a not-found error, and no changes should occur in the database. The scenario validates proper error handling for not-found resources.

Test that update attempts by users without admin privileges are denied. Attempt to update another user's member record as a non-admin (e.g., as a member or guest). The API should respond with a permission-denied error, and audit logs should capture the attempted violation. No changes should be made to the member record.

dependencies.purpose: Provision a test member record to target for the invalid-permission update.

scenario.draft: Test update failure due to invalid input data. Provide a request body that violates schema constraints—for example, missing required updatable fields, providing null for non-nullable fields, or invalid data types. The system should return a validation error, and the member record should remain unchanged in the database.

dependencies.purpose: Provision a member to be used in the invalid update request, ensuring there's a real memberId.

scenario.draft: Test successful hard deletion of a membership record by admin. Begin by creating a new member with admin role, then request DELETE with the member's id. Verify that the record is completely removed from the system (hard delete), no longer appears in queries, and any attempt to fetch the deleted record returns not found.

dependencies.purpose: Create a member record to serve as the target for deletion and ensure valid test context.

scenario.draft: Test error handling when attempting to delete a non-existent or random UUID as memberId. The system should respond with a not-found error and ensure there are no unintended deletions or changes to other member records.

Test that only admins can delete member records. Attempt deletion by a non-admin user and confirm that permission is denied, the database is unchanged, and an audit event is logged regarding the failed attempt.

dependencies.purpose: Provision a member record for the deletion test, targeting enforcement of role-based permissions.

scenario.draft: Test successful retrieval of the full guest session list as an admin. Ensure that there are one or more guest records in the system—if not, create guest sessions beforehand. Send a GET request and verify the complete list of guest session objects matches those stored. The test should confirm all required fields are present in the response and that only admins can view all data.

dependencies.purpose: Create one or more guest session records to ensure the system under test has retrievable guest data.

scenario.draft: Ensure that non-admin users (guests, members, moderators) cannot access the guest session list via the admin endpoint. Attempt to retrieve the list as a non-admin and expect an access-denied response. Confirm there is no data leakage of guest analytics to unauthorized users.

Test the system's response when no guest records exist. As an admin, request the guest session list on an empty database. The response should be a valid but empty list, and no error should occur. This validates system behavior under an empty dataset.

Test successful advanced search and filtering over guest sessions as admin. First, create several guest session records with varying first_seen and last_seen timestamps, and session_identifiers. Issue a PATCH request with valid filters (by session_identifier or date range). Validate that only matching guest sessions are returned and results are correctly paginated and sorted as per request.

dependencies.purpose: Insert multiple guest sessions with varying field values to serve as search/filter test data.

scenario.draft: Test error handling for malformed or invalid filter parameters. Send a PATCH search request with invalid field names, values out of range, or incorrect types. Validate that the system responds with a validation or error message and no guest session records are returned.

Verify that non-admin roles cannot perform advanced searches over guest analytics. Attempt to PATCH search as a guest, member, or moderator and confirm that an appropriate permission-denied error is returned.

Test retrieving a guest session by its unique guestId. First, create a guest record, then fetch it by its id as an admin. Confirm the returned data includes the full detail for the correct guest session, and the fields match what was inserted.

dependencies.purpose: Create a test guest session to be used for the targeted fetch operation, ensuring the existence of a valid guestId.

scenario.draft: Test error handling for attempts to fetch a guest session with a random or invalid UUID. Issue a GET request using a non-existent or malformed guestId and confirm the system responds with a not-found error and no data is inadvertently returned.

Check that only admins can access guest session details using this endpoint. Attempt access as a non-admin, and confirm an access-denied error is received and no guest session information is revealed.

Test that a member can successfully retrieve the full details of an active, public system notice by its UUID using this endpoint. First, ensure that a system notice is created and marked as active by an admin. Then, as a member, attempt to fetch the notice via its UUID. Validate that all expected fields (title, body, category association, status, scheduling) are present in the response and correspond to the persisted data. Ensure that public and currently active status is respected, making the notice visible to members. Edge case: try to fetch a non-existent notice and verify that an appropriate 404 or error message is returned.

dependencies.purpose: Create an active system notice as data setup, since only admins can create notices.

scenario.draft: Test that a member cannot retrieve a system notice that is inactive, expired, or scheduled for the future. First, create a notice as inactive or with scheduling outside the current date. Attempt to fetch the notice as a member and expect an error or appropriate denial indicating insufficient visibility. Confirm that only eligible active notices are accessible through this endpoint.

dependencies.purpose: Create an inactive or scheduled (future) system notice to be tested for visibility restrictions.

scenario.draft: Verify that an admin user can successfully create a new system notice with valid fields (title, body, is_active, and optional category/scheduling). Check that the response includes a generated UUID, timestamps, and correct association with any referenced category. Validate that the created notice is retrievable by ID and visible according to its is_active/schedule settings.

Test failure when attempting to create a notice with a category_id that does not exist. The system should reject the creation and return a clear error message about the invalid category reference. Validate that no new notice is created in this case.

Test creation logic enforcing uniqueness of notice titles within the same category. First, create a notice with a specific title under a category. Then attempt to create another notice with the same title in the same category. Expect a validation error about duplicate title. Changing the category or title should allow creation.

dependencies.purpose: Create the initial system notice to set up a duplicate title error in the same category.

scenario.draft: Verify an admin can update an existing system notice by its UUID, modifying fields such as title, body, status, scheduling, and associated category. The notice should reflect the updated values on retrieval and in subsequent listings. Validate correct audit logging (if exposed) and ensure all field-level validation (e.g., valid schedule logic, unique title per category) applies.

dependencies.purpose: Create a system notice to be updated in this scenario.

scenario.draft: Test the failure scenario where an admin attempts to update a system notice with an invalid scheduling window (start_at after end_at). The API should reject the update and return a validation error specifying the scheduling logic violation. Ensure the original notice fields remain unchanged after the failed operation.

dependencies.purpose: Create a system notice as a prerequisite for testing a schedule validation error.

scenario.draft: Validate that an admin can successfully delete an existing system notice using its UUID. First, create a system notice to ensure a known record exists. Then perform the DELETE and verify the notice is no longer retrievable by ID. Confirm that deletion is irreversible and is audit-logged (if possible). Try retrieving the deleted notice and expect a 404 or not found error.

dependencies.purpose: Create the system notice that will be deleted in this scenario.

scenario.draft: Verify that an admin can retrieve the full paginated list of currently registered and historical administrators. The response should include all necessary metadata (UUID, user_identifier, grant/revoke timestamps) without any sensitive or extraneous data. Confirm that revoked (inactive) and currently active admins are both included, and no filtering/sorting is applied by default.

Fetch a specific engagement stat by known valid ID as an admin. The system should return the correct detailed record matching the ID. Validate all returned fields and ensure representation matches the persisted record. This is a basic happy path retrieval scenario.

dependencies.purpose: Create a sample engagement stat record and take its ID to use for detail retrieval.

scenario.draft: Attempt to retrieve an engagement statistic using a nonexistent or invalid ID. The system must return a 404 not found error or equivalent message, and must not leak any data about other records.

Successfully create a new engagement statistics record with all required fields filled according to the schema, using a valid reporting period, dimensions, and count values. The record should be retrievable afterward via the detail and search APIs. This validates positive creation and persistence.

Attempt to create an engagement statistic entry with critical missing or invalid fields (such as omitting period, dimension, or providing negative or non-numeric counts). Verify that the API validates input, rejects the record, and returns suitable error messages for each business rule violation.

Update an existing engagement stat record by changing allowable fields (such as adjusting user activity, post count, or time period). The response should show the updated values, and repeated retrieval should confirm persistence. All business rules for field updates (such as uniqueness, valid ranges) must be enforced.

dependencies.purpose: Create an engagement stat record to obtain a valid ID for update.

scenario.draft: Attempt to update a stat with data that violates schema constraints (such as setting a period that overlaps another stat, using negative counts, or missing required fields). The system must prevent the update and return a clear error response.

dependencies.purpose: Create an original engagement stat record as the basis for attempted invalid update.

scenario.draft: Delete an existing engagement stat record by its ID as an admin. The deletion must be permanent (as no soft-delete exists), and subsequent retrieval with the same ID should return a 404 not found error. All deletion events must be fully compliant with audit expectations.

dependencies.purpose: Insert a new engagement stat record to acquire a valid ID to be deleted.

scenario.draft: Attempt to delete an engagement stat using a nonexistent or already-deleted ID. Must verify that the system returns an appropriate not found or error message, and no unintended effects occur.

Test that an admin user can retrieve the full list of comments on the discussion board, including both active and deleted comments, as authorized by admin privileges. Confirm pagination, expected summary fields, and presence of deletion markers for soft-deleted comments. Validate that sensitive content is appropriately handled. The test requires at least one active and one deleted comment in the database.

dependencies.purpose: Create a new member account to generate comments with a known author for visibility in the listing.
Post a topic under which comments can be created and tested.
Post a thread for comments association.
Add a post (parent for comments) so comments can be tested.
Create at least two comments (one to remain active, one to later soft-delete for deletion visibility test).
Soft-delete one of the comments created, marking is_deleted to test listing of deleted comments.

scenario.draft: Test that a moderator can retrieve the complete comment list, covering both active and deleted comments. Confirm that moderation privileges allow the viewing of deleted content, and that sensitive/private information is not exposed beyond the expected comment fields. Check pagination and summary structure. Requires comments present in various states.

dependencies.purpose: Create a board member so that comments on the platform can be generated for comprehensive listing.
Provide a discussion topic under which test comments can be made.
Establish a thread for assigning test comments.
Create a parent post to which comments will be attached.
Insert test comments so there is content for the listing, including a comment marked deleted for moderation evaluation.
Convert one comment to deleted state for verification of moderator listing permissions.

scenario.draft: Test that an admin can perform advanced searches on comments using filters such as content keywords and date ranges. Validate correct results are returned for simple and compound filters, including paginated results. Make sure only comments within the filtered criteria and within admin's privileges appear. Check for cases with no results as well.

dependencies.purpose: Provision a member to own comments with known content and timestamps for reliable filtering tests.
Create a topic for placing posts and comments.
Add a thread for targeted post and comment operations.
Create a post for attaching comments to, allowing controlled test data creation.
Create multiple comments with distinct known contents and timestamps to be used in search filtering tests.

scenario.draft: Verify that when an admin searches with filters for a specific member ID and soft-deleted status, the resulting comment list contains only comments written by that member and reflecting their is_deleted status. Validate edge cases of no matching results and pagination across deleted and active comments.

dependencies.purpose: Create a member whose ID will be used as a filter for search queries.
Add a topic for creating context.
Add a thread to use as a parent for posts/comments.
Create a post under which comments will be added for the member, including some later soft-deleted.
Generate comments for the specific member, including at least one normal and one to be soft-deleted by update.
Soft-delete a member's comment so the filter for is_deleted can yield results.

scenario.draft: Test moderator advanced search and filtering for comments based on text (content) keywords. Ensure search returns only comments with matching keywords. Verify results honor soft-deleted visibility for the moderator role. Paginated results must be thoroughly checked.

dependencies.purpose: Provision a test member to create comments containing specific keywords.
Provide a topic for comment context.
Create a thread for post/comment assignment.
Produce a post attached to the thread, allowing comments to be tied to specific text.
Add several comments with varying content for use in search.

scenario.draft: Test moderator's ability to filter and paginate comments based on deletion status (is_deleted) and created/updated date ranges. Confirm only proper comments are returned, and ensure both deleted and non-deleted comments can be discovered, including edge cases with no matches.

dependencies.purpose: Add test member for controlled comment creation.
Establish a context topic.
Thread for managing posts/comments.
Generate post where comments can be tested.
Insert comments for the test, some to be marked deleted.
Soft-delete one comment to enable is_deleted filter evaluation.

scenario.draft: Ensure that an admin can fetch full details for a single comment using its unique id. Validate that the correct comment is returned with all schema-defined fields, including is_deleted status, content, member reference, post reference, and timestamps. Confirm that sensitive or privileged information is appropriately masked and correct error returned for invalid UUID.

dependencies.purpose: Create a test member to author the comment to be fetched by id.
Insert a topic for contextual placement.
Provide a thread to attach posts/comments.
Post to which the comment will belong.
Create the comment and obtain its commentId for testing fetch by valid id.

scenario.draft: Confirm that attempting to fetch a comment with an invalid, non-existent, or improperly formatted id returns a user-friendly not found or validation error. This covers edge case error handling for comment lookup.

Test successful thread creation as an admin under an existing, open topic. First, ensure an admin member exists and logs in, then as admin create a new topic using the respective endpoint (make sure the topic is open for new threads). After that, call this endpoint to create a new thread with a unique title. Verify the response includes all required thread fields and is associated with the correct topic and creator. Confirm the thread appears in the topic's thread list.

dependencies.purpose: Create an admin member who can act as the creator for topics/threads.
Create a new topic as an admin for use as the parent for thread creation.

scenario.draft: Test thread creation in a topic that is closed to new threads. First, as admin, create a topic, then update the topic to set its closed flag to true. Then attempt to create a thread under the closed topic and verify the operation fails with a business rule violation (cannot create thread in closed topic).

dependencies.purpose: Create an admin member to act as creator/context for the topic and thread.
Create a new topic.
Set the topic's closed flag to true (updating the topic to be closed before thread creation attempt).

scenario.draft: Test failure when attempting to create a thread with a duplicate title within a topic. First, create a topic, then create a thread with a specific title. Attempt to create another thread with the same title under the same topic and confirm that the business logic enforces unique thread titles within a topic, returning a duplicate error.

dependencies.purpose: Create an admin member to be the acting user and thread creator.
Create a new topic as the parent.
Create the initial thread with a specific title to establish the duplicate condition.

scenario.draft: Test error response when trying to create a thread under a non-existent topic. Attempt to call the endpoint with a random or deleted topicId and confirm that the API returns a 404 not found or equivalent error message.

dependencies.purpose: Provision an admin user for authorization, even if the topic does not exist.

scenario.draft: Test successful update of a thread's title by the original thread creator (member). First, register a member, create a topic, then have the member create a thread. Next, as the thread owner, call the update endpoint to set a new unique title. Confirm the response reflects the updated thread, the changes are persisted, and audit logs (if available) attribute the update to the correct user.

dependencies.purpose: Register or create the member user who will be the thread creator.
Create the parent topic for thread creation.
Member creates the initial thread to be updated.

scenario.draft: Test business rule validation that prevents updating a thread's title to a duplicate of another thread within the same topic. Create a topic, add two threads with unique titles, then attempt to update the second thread's title to match the first. Confirm the API rejects the update and returns a duplicate error.

dependencies.purpose: Register a member user who can create and attempt to update threads.
Create the topic for thread operations.
Create both threads with unique titles for duplication test.

scenario.draft: Verify that an unauthorized member (not the thread creator) cannot update another member's thread. Create two member users, a topic, have one member create a thread, and attempt to update the thread as the other member. Confirm that the API denies the update due to lack of ownership or permission.

dependencies.purpose: Register Member A (thread creator).
Register Member B (unauthorized updater).
Create the topic for the threads.
Have Member A create the thread.

scenario.draft: Test that a moderator can update any thread within a topic, regardless of original thread ownership. Register a moderator, create a topic, let a member create a thread, then as the moderator update the thread's title. Verify the changes are applied and audit trails are correct.

dependencies.purpose: Create or register a moderator user.
Register a member to create the thread.
Establish the parent topic for the thread.
Have the member create the thread to be updated by the moderator.

scenario.draft: Test that a moderator cannot update a thread with an invalid or empty title (business validation). Attempt to update as moderator with a blank or too-long title, and confirm the API returns input validation errors.

dependencies.purpose: Create a moderator user.
Register a member as thread creator.
Create the topic for thread operations.
Member creates the thread.

scenario.draft: Test that an admin can update any thread's core fields within any topic. Register an admin, member, and topic; have the member create a thread, then as admin, update the thread. Confirm the thread's fields are updated and changes are reflected in subsequent fetches.

dependencies.purpose: Register an admin user.
Register a member who will create the thread.
Create the target topic.
Member creates thread to be updated by admin.

scenario.draft: Test error handling when the admin attempts to update a non-existent thread. Attempt the update with random or deleted threadId and verify the endpoint returns a not found error.

dependencies.purpose: Register an admin user to perform the update.
Create a topic context if required for errors.

scenario.draft: Test successful deletion of a thread by a moderator. Set up moderator, member, and topic, have the member create a thread, then as moderator delete the thread. Confirm the thread is no longer available in the topic's thread list and all cascading deletes are effective.

dependencies.purpose: Register moderator user.
Register member (thread creator).
Create the topic where the thread is created.
Member creates thread for moderator to delete.

scenario.draft: Test that a regular member cannot delete a thread via the moderator endpoint (unauthorized access). Register member, moderator, and topic; have member create a thread; then attempt to delete as the unauthorized member and confirm that access is denied.

dependencies.purpose: Register a member for thread creation.
Register a moderator for authorization comparison.
Create a topic.
Member creates a thread to attempt unauthorized deletion.

scenario.draft: Scenario: A moderator creates a new flag on a specific post indicating a potential violation of community guidelines. The moderator selects a valid post ID, specifies the flag type (e.g., spam or abuse), provides a source (manual), and adds an optional note. The API should create the content flag and return the full flag record for tracking. Prerequisite: The target post must exist, and the acting user should have moderator privileges.

dependencies.purpose: Create a valid post as the flag target. The post must exist and be accessible to the moderator account before flagging.
Assign moderator role to a user, ensuring authorization to perform flag creation.

scenario.draft: Scenario: A moderator attempts to create a content flag with the same type on the same post more than once, triggering a uniqueness constraint. The first flag creation completes successfully. On the duplicate creation attempt (same post, type, and source), the API should reject the request, returning a meaningful error about duplicate flag constraints. This ensures that multiple identical flags for the same issue are not allowed. Prerequisites: Post exists and a moderator is authenticated.

dependencies.purpose: Create the post to be flagged. Required for associating flags to the specific post.
Assign moderator privileges to the test user.
Create the first content flag to establish the duplicate condition for the follow-up request.

scenario.draft: Scenario: A moderator attempts to create a content flag using a post_id or comment_id that does not exist in the system. The API should reject the request, responding with an error indicating that the target entity was not found, and no flag is created. This validates referential integrity and error reporting for invalid flag targets.

dependencies.purpose: Assign moderator role so user can attempt flag creation with arbitrary non-existent post/comment ID.

scenario.draft: Scenario: An admin creates a new moderation flag on a comment to mark it for review. The admin specifies a valid comment_id, selects the appropriate flag type (e.g., inappropriate), and submits the request. On success, the API creates the new flag and returns the full record for referencing in future moderation actions. Prerequisites: The comment must exist, and the user must have admin authorization.

dependencies.purpose: Create a valid comment to serve as the flag target.
Grant admin privileges to a user for authorization to perform the flag operation.

scenario.draft: Scenario: A user without moderator or admin privileges attempts to create a content flag via the admin endpoint. The API must reject this request, returning an authorization error confirming that only privileged roles can create content flags. The system audit log should capture this failed permission check. Prerequisites: Test user exists but does NOT have moderator or admin privileges.

dependencies.purpose: Create a comment to attempt flagging as an unauthorized user.
Register a member user to attempt the unauthorized action.

scenario.draft: Scenario: A moderator reviews an active content flag on a post and updates its status to cleared, indicating resolution. The moderator is authenticated, provides the update (such as cleared=true or status="resolved" in the payload), and the API returns the updated flag record reflecting the changes. This scenario verifies that flag lifecycle state transitions are functioning and auditable. Prerequisites: The flagged post exists, and the moderator has access.

dependencies.purpose: Create and persist a post to serve as the flag target.
Assign moderator rights so the update is authorized.
Create a content flag on the target post to set up a modifiable flag context.

scenario.draft: Scenario: Moderator attempts to update an existing content flag but provides an invalid update, such as an unrecognized flag type or missing required field. The API should reject the request and return a validation or business logic error based on the schema. This ensures only valid updates are accepted and error handling is clear. Prerequisites: Need an existing flag and authenticated moderator; the payload is deliberately incorrect.

dependencies.purpose: Create a post as the flag target.
Authorize user as moderator for update access.
Create an initial content flag to update in the negative test scenario.

scenario.draft: Scenario: An admin updates an existing content flag to amend the type, add resolution notes, or clear the flag after reviewing. The admin provides a valid update payload and receives a full updated flag record on success. All changes are audit-logged. Prerequisites: Create a target comment, then flag it, and ensure the user is an admin.

dependencies.purpose: Prepare a comment to be flagged.
Create/administer an admin account for authorization.
Create a content flag as setup for the update test.

scenario.draft: Scenario: A user who is not an admin attempts to update a content flag, for example to clear or modify its status/type. The API must deny the request due to insufficient privileges and return an appropriate authorization error. Prerequisites: A flag is created, and an ordinary member (not admin) attempts a flag update.

dependencies.purpose: Have a comment available for flagging and testing.
Create the flag as update target.
Create a regular member account for the unauthorized update attempt.

scenario.draft: Scenario: A moderator deletes (hard deletes) a content flag after resolving the issue or upon review. The API must remove the flag record from the database, and no subsequent retrieval should be possible. Audit logs should reflect the deletion. Prerequisites: Moderator privilege and an existing flag for deletion; deletion is irreversible.

dependencies.purpose: Ensure a post exists to be flagged.
Grant moderator role for authorization.
Create a flag on the post to serve as the deletion candidate.

scenario.draft: Scenario: A user lacking moderator or admin privileges attempts to delete a content flag. The API must deny the request, returning an appropriate authorization error, and the flag must remain in the system unchanged. Prerequisites: Prepare a flag, and ensure deletion is attempted by a non-privileged member user.

dependencies.purpose: Create a post to associate with the flag.
Create a flag to be the deletion target.
Create a normal member user for the unauthorized deletion attempt.

scenario.draft: Test that a moderator can successfully update a specific version of a comment. Precondition: an existing comment with multiple versions, where at least one version exists. The moderator attempts to change the content snapshot for one particular version. The expected outcome is that the update is committed and reflected in version history, with updated audit fields. Dependencies: comment and version creation endpoints.

dependencies.purpose: Create a comment as a member to serve as the target for versioning and moderation.
Add a version to the comment so that an existing version can be updated by the moderator.

scenario.draft: Test that the moderator receives an error when attempting to update a comment version using a non-existent commentId or versionId. The scenario involves providing invalid UUIDs for either the comment or version. The expected response is a clear error message indicating not found. Dependencies: none needed for invalid ID test, but detail about error handling is verified.

Test that attempting to update a comment version as a user without moderator/admin privileges is forbidden. The scenario begins with a member creating a comment and version, followed by a non-privileged actor trying to update a version. The operation should fail and return an authorization error. Dependencies: comment creation, version creation, and simulation of session context as a non-privileged user.

dependencies.purpose: Create a comment and version as a member for update attempt.
Create a version for the comment to attempt to update as a non-moderator.

scenario.draft: Verify that an admin can update a comment version's content snapshot. Precondition: there are comments with multiple versions. The admin user sends updated content for one version. Success is indicated by the persistence of the changes and updated audit fields. Dependencies: comment and version creation endpoints.

dependencies.purpose: Create a comment for which a version will be added.
Create a version to be updated by the admin.

scenario.draft: Attempt to update a comment version with invalid commentId or versionId as an admin. The scenario checks that the system returns appropriate not found errors for incorrect references.

Ensure that a user without admin or moderator privileges (e.g., a member) cannot use the admin endpoint to update a comment version. The test expects an authorization failure response. Preconditions: create a comment and version; attempt update as unauthorized user.

dependencies.purpose: Create the base comment for versioning.
Add a version to attempt update as a non-admin user.

scenario.draft: Simulate an admin hard-deleting a specific comment version. Precondition: a comment with multiple versions exists. The designated version is deleted. The system should remove the version entry from history, maintain audit logs, and update UI views accordingly. Dependencies include comment and version creation endpoints.

dependencies.purpose: Create a comment and add at least two versions so one can be deleted.
Add a version to the comment for deletion.

scenario.draft: Test that deleting a version using an invalid commentId or versionId returns a not found error, ensuring the system properly handles references to non-existent records.

Verify that only admins can delete comment versions using the admin endpoint. A non-admin user attempts this operation and receives an authorization error. Precondition: a comment and at least one version exist.

dependencies.purpose: Create the base comment for the version.
Add a version to attempt unauthorized deletion.

scenario.draft: Test that a member who owns a comment can retrieve a list of all attachments associated with their comment. Comment must exist and have at least one attachment. Dependencies: comment creation, attachment creation endpoints.

dependencies.purpose: Create a member-owned comment for attachment.
Add at least one attachment to the comment.

scenario.draft: Test the case where a member tries to list attachments for a commentId that does not exist. The expected outcome is a clear not found error response.

Test that a member who does not own the comment cannot list attachments for another user's comment if privacy restrictions apply. Preconditions: create a comment as member A, attempt to list attachments as member B (not owner nor moderator/admin). Expect a permission denied or filtered result. Dependencies: comment creation and session setup for different users.

dependencies.purpose: Create a comment as member A for ownership test.
Add an attachment to the comment owned by member A.

scenario.draft: Verify that a moderator can retrieve all attachments for a specific comment, including those on comments owned by other users. The comment and at least one attachment must exist. The test confirms access and response accuracy. Dependencies: comment and attachment creation endpoints.

dependencies.purpose: Create a comment with attachments for the moderator to retrieve.
Add one or more attachments to the comment for viewing.

scenario.draft: Attempt to access attachments using a non-existent commentId as a moderator. Confirm that a not found error is returned and no data is leaked.

Ensure that a moderator can view attachments for any comment, even if the comment is private or restricted to the original owner. This verifies elevated privileges of moderators. The scenario includes comment and attachment creation and moderator access.

dependencies.purpose: Create a comment whose attachments are restricted for members but should be visible to moderators.
Add restricted attachment to the comment for moderator access validation.

scenario.draft: Verify that a user (guest or authenticated) can successfully retrieve a paginated list of threads for an existing topic. The topic must exist and be active. The response should include summary details for all threads belonging to the specified topic, respecting pagination parameters. The test ensures only threads belonging to the specified topic are included and pagination works as expected.

dependencies.purpose: Fetch details of the topic to confirm it exists and extract its topicId for use in retrieving threads.
Create one or more threads in the topic as test data to ensure there are threads to return in the list.

scenario.draft: Test that attempting to list threads for a non-existent topicId returns an appropriate not found error. The system should not return threads or an empty result, but an explicit error indicating the topic does not exist.

Validate that when a topic exists but has no threads, the endpoint returns an empty list in the paginated response. No error should occur; the response should be a paginated structure with zero entries.

dependencies.purpose: Confirm the existence of a topic and verify it is new or empty. Use this topic's topicId in the test.

scenario.draft: Test searching for threads by partial or full title match within a topic. First, create a topic and several threads with varying titles (some containing the search term, others not). Submit a PATCH request with a search parameter for the title and verify the result only includes threads whose titles match the search. Verify pagination, sorting, and that irrelevant threads are excluded.

dependencies.purpose: Create test threads with specific titles to enable meaningful search filtering.

scenario.draft: Verify that searching for threads within a topic using criteria that match no threads (e.g., non-existent keywords or creator) returns a paginated response with zero results, not an error.

dependencies.purpose: Ensure a valid topic exists for the search operation.

scenario.draft: Attempt to search threads using an invalid or non-existent topicId and verify that a clear error response is returned, rather than a silent empty result.

Test retrieving the full details for a specific thread under a topic. Create a new topic and a thread within it, then request the thread detail. Validate that the details match the data used to create the thread, and all relationships (topic, creator) are correctly reflected.

dependencies.purpose: Create a thread under a topic to ensure there is valid data for the lookup.

scenario.draft: Attempt to retrieve a thread with a non-existent or invalid threadId under a valid topic. Confirm that the API returns an appropriate not found error and does not leak any internal state or unrelated information.

dependencies.purpose: Ensure the topic exists and is valid to isolate the error condition to the threadId.

scenario.draft: Try retrieving a thread using a valid threadId but with a topicId that does not match the thread's actual parent topic. The system should return an error, confirming referential integrity and ID relationship enforcement.

dependencies.purpose: Create a thread to obtain a valid threadId and its parent topicId for cross-check testing.
Set up a second topic with a different topicId for use as a mismatched parent in the test.

scenario.draft: Verify that an authenticated member can create a thread under an existing, active topic. All required fields (title, topicId, creator info) must be present and valid. The test validates successful thread creation and ensures response data matches the request.

dependencies.purpose: Ensure a valid topic exists. Extract topicId for use in thread creation.

scenario.draft: Attempt to create a thread in a topic that is closed (no longer accepting threads). The system should reject the request and return an error indicating that the topic is closed for new threads.

dependencies.purpose: Create or update a topic and mark it as closed, then attempt thread creation to validate business rule enforcement.

scenario.draft: Check that trying to create two threads with the same title under the same topic fails on the second attempt, returning an error about title uniqueness per topic as enforced in the schema.

dependencies.purpose: Confirm topic exists.
Create an initial thread with a distinct title to prepare for a duplicate creation attempt.

scenario.draft: Try to create a thread using a topicId that does not exist or is invalid, expecting an explicit error about the missing or invalid topic reference.

Ensure that a user with moderator privileges can successfully create a thread in an existing topic, following the same rules and validations as a regular member but with elevated permissions. Response should include the created thread's information.

dependencies.purpose: Confirm a valid, active topic exists to enable thread creation as a moderator.

scenario.draft: Attempt to create a thread as a moderator in a topic marked as closed. The API should still enforce the closed status and return a business rule error, confirming that even privileged roles cannot override topic closure via this API.

dependencies.purpose: Create or update a topic and set its status to closed. Use this topicId to test that moderator creation is denied.

scenario.draft: Check that a moderator attempting to create two threads with the same title under one topic receives a uniqueness error for the second creation, proving that title duplication is prevented across all roles.

dependencies.purpose: Confirm a topic exists for the test.
Create a first thread with a unique title before attempting duplicate creation as moderator.

scenario.draft: Ensure that creating a thread as a moderator in a non-existent or invalid topic ID will result in a proper not found error, confirming referential and existence checks for thread creation.

Test retrieving the list of attachments for a post that has multiple attachments. First, create a member and an associated post. Then, upload multiple attachments to the post using the member's authentication. Finally, call the GET endpoint to verify that all uploaded attachments are correctly returned in the response, including their metadata (filename, mime type, upload time, etc.).

dependencies.purpose: Create a post to attach files to. Requires valid member and thread context.
Upload one or more attachments to the created post to set up the test condition.

scenario.draft: Test retrieving the list of attachments for a post that has no attachments. Start by creating a member and a post without uploading any attachments. Call the GET endpoint and verify that it returns an empty list, confirming no attachments are present for that post.

dependencies.purpose: Create a post without attachments. Valid member and thread setup needed.

scenario.draft: Test searching attachments on a post by filename and MIME type. First, create a member, post, and upload several attachments with distinct filenames and types. Use the PATCH endpoint with search filters for a particular filename fragment and MIME type, and verify the returned list includes only matching attachments.

dependencies.purpose: Create a new post to attach files to for test setup.
Upload multiple attachments with varied metadata to establish search test conditions.

scenario.draft: Test searching for attachments using filters that do not match any attachments. Create a member, post, and upload some attachments. Then search using a rare or non-existent filename or MIME type and verify the response returns an empty list.

dependencies.purpose: Create a post as context for attachments.
Add attachments to the post for negative search scenario.

scenario.draft: Test failure case when submitting an invalid or malformed search query on attachments. Attempt to search with invalid data (e.g., unsupported filters, improperly formatted date ranges) and verify that the API returns a user-friendly error response indicating the nature of the problem.

dependencies.purpose: Create a post for context. Attachment uploads may be optional here.

scenario.draft: Test retrieving metadata about a single attachment by its attachmentId and parent postId. Ensure the attachment exists by first creating a post and uploading an attachment. Confirm that the GET call returns accurate metadata including filename, file URI, uploader, MIME type, and timestamp.

dependencies.purpose: Create a new post for attachment context.
Upload a new attachment and retrieve the ID for use in metadata retrieval.

scenario.draft: Test failure when attempting to get details for an attachmentId that does not exist on a valid post. Create a post with valid member context but do not upload an attachment with the tested ID. Call the endpoint with a random or incorrect attachmentId and confirm a not found or error response is returned.

dependencies.purpose: Create a parent post.

scenario.draft: Test successful upload and creation of an attachment on a post. Create a member, post, and then call this endpoint to upload a valid file attachment. Verify that the response contains accurate metadata including file URI, name, type, and that the attachment is linked to the correct post. Also ensure permissions are enforced.

dependencies.purpose: Create a post that will accept attachments.

scenario.draft: Test failure when uploading an attachment with a file type or MIME type disallowed by business rules. Attempt to upload a file with an unsupported extension or MIME and confirm the operation fails with an error explaining the violation.

dependencies.purpose: Set up the post for attachment upload.

scenario.draft: Test uploading an attachment as a user who is not permitted (e.g., not the post owner, or in a locked post). Attempt to upload an attachment as a different member or to a post in a locked state, and verify access is denied with an appropriate error message.

dependencies.purpose: Create the post context for a permission denial scenario.

scenario.draft: Test updating file metadata (such as file name) for an attachment by the original member/uploader. Create a member, post, upload an attachment, and then use the PUT endpoint to modify allowed metadata. Confirm changes are reflected in the response and are stored.

dependencies.purpose: Create the post hosting the attachment.
Upload an attachment to provide an updatable target.

scenario.draft: Test authorization failure when a user who did not upload the attachment attempts to update its metadata. Create an attachment with a member, then attempt update from a different member account. Confirm operation is denied and returns an appropriate error response.

dependencies.purpose: Create the post context and first attachment as owner.
Create initial attachment as owner. Additional member can be created as needed.

scenario.draft: Test error response when attempting to update metadata for an attachment that does not exist. Attempt to update using a random or invalid attachmentId (on a valid post), and validate an appropriate error is returned indicating the attachment cannot be found.

dependencies.purpose: Create the post for the update test context.

scenario.draft: Test a successful update of a comment attachment's metadata (such as file name or URI) by the attachment's original uploader (member role). First, create a member and have them add a new comment under a post. Then, upload an attachment to this comment using the member account. Attempt to update modifiable metadata fields of this attachment, such as the attachment name or the download URI. Verify the operation succeeds and the updated metadata is returned. The scenario should validate that only fields allowed by business rules are changed, and that immutable properties (like upload timestamp) remain unchanged.

dependencies.purpose: Create a member account who will own the comment and attachment.
Add a new comment as the member to associate the attachment with.
